source_visual_beats.description: Vey attempts to mate a Zoran field crystal to a utility walker. Its facets do not align with the Nyssarian socket; the control glyphs chatter and go dark. Both crystals remain in the handling systems appropriate to their cultures.

A Zoran crystal keeper explains the engineering mismatch: Zoran field crystals are conditioned to release mana in responsive pulses, while Nyssarian regulators expect a rigid, clocked flow. Neither crystal system is defective; the difference lies in conditioning and regulation rather than the mana itself.

source_visual_beats.description: At the western aerodrome stands the huge balloon once used to carry Tech-Mech Prototype 01 over the mountains. Its torn lifting harness still hangs beneath it.

Chairman M'ow Oh, still the civilian head of Nyas but unable to assemble a cabinet quorum, sends a provisional envoy to propose using the balloon to fetch a Zoran delegation. The proposal carries his emergency command seal and the municipal council's co-signature; ground routes are blocked, and ordinary aircraft lack fuel and range.

source_visual_beats.description: After the failed charge and the death in Low Basin, Vey asks Midori to help create a physical energy ledger rather than treating her as a power source: every charge receives a purpose, expected loss, operator, crystal condition, and reserve estimate. Midori agrees because memory and good intentions did not restrain her; a record others can challenge might.
Testing shows fast transfers waste more mana and contaminate the lattice. Damaged conduits waste still more. Rest periods reduce feedback into Midori.

segments: After Midori’s expedition departed, May Jin volunteered to serve as an interpreter.
The Temple custodians and Zoran rear command amended his parole together, then moved him under guard with a supply convoy.
He reached the rear headquarters before the crisis in Nyas began and has spent the local cease-fire translating prisoner lists and explaining Nyssarian command codes.

pages.title: THE MAN WHO GAVE THE ORDER

source_visual_beats.description: Orin opens the warehouse records cage under civilian witnesses. May Jin authenticates its fire-control log against the captured codebook, serial seals, and command phrases he translated for Zora. The chain of custody identifies Colonel Rauk, commander of the Mana Bomb targeting bureau and the artillery group that selected the refugee approach as a suppression zone.

His signed orders tied the bomb deployment to the barrage pattern that killed Adnil and Marta. He was not a random Tech-Mech officer; he approved the target solution after civilian movement was reported.

source_visual_beats.description: Images overlap: Adnil, Marta, the dead runner, the thirsty grandfather, the burned Nyssarian boy, Sela beside the poisoned basin, Vey breaking the charge, and Hanae saving Buren. The dead still feel like a command to strike; the living now give her competing reasons to stop.
M'ow Oh arrives unarmed after his envoy reports both the attempted extraction and Midori's loss of control. He orders Nyssarian weapons lowered before stepping into the edge of the field.

source_visual_beats.description: Midori does not stop because M’ow Oh absolves her or because the anger passes. She sees the shelter entrance behind him, remembers the people who accepted responsibility for restraining her power, and chooses to honor that dependence. She collapses the field inward and grounds it into an empty artillery pit. The blast leaves her barely conscious and permanently reduces the reserve.

source_visual_beats.description: Midori wakes in North Hospital beside the people she nearly endangered. Hanae tells her the truth: no civilians died from the field, but several were injured in the panic.

Midori asks what she owes the people she frightened and injured. A wounded mother refuses her apology and says the debt cannot be settled in this room; another thanks her for stopping. Midori accepts both answers without asking either woman to repair her guilt.

source_visual_beats.description: Chairman M'ow Oh summons Midori to Crown Heights under a civilian safe-conduct co-signed by the municipal council, the Civil Relief Assembly, and Zoran command. The document identifies him as Nyas's civilian head and emergency commander-in-chief while recording that his cabinet quorum and control of field units remain disputed.

Midori insists that Buren, May Jin, Sela, Hanae, Orin, and Vey attend in defined roles. M'ow Oh accepts all six: Buren and May Jin as working participants, and the four civilian officials as accredited observers in the adjoining gallery.

source_visual_beats.description: Kesh privately offers information about a portal that may give Midori a path home. Kesh insists that surrender will leave Nyas defenseless against vengeance, but her proposed remedy is to let the cabinet escape: Midori must abandon the surrender demand and guarantee their passage.
No one tours the portal, tests it, or negotiates its ownership. Its destination and safety remain unknown; it is only a promise used as leverage.

source_visual_beats.description: The offer awakens Midori’s older wound: Truk’s cruelty, the executions he ordered, and the human world she was torn from. For a moment, the portal feels like permission to abandon Nyas, Zora, the ledger, and every person who has acquired a claim on her choices.

She separates the enemies she had collapsed together. Rauk and Nyas can answer for this war; neither can answer for Truk. Revenge against Nyas would spend lives needed to stop the war and still leave the older wound untouched.

source_visual_beats.description: Hardliners circulate claims that Geroff intends mass executions. Zoran soldiers hear a second rumor that Nyas has hidden another Mana Bomb. Both claims spread faster than the bilingual notices correcting them; the bomb rumor is false.

May Jin, Orin, and Zoran record keepers publish a parallel statement in canonical Nyssarian and Zoran scripts listing the narrow subjects of the next day’s meeting: cessation of organized combat, custody of heavy weapons, aid access, and command compliance. Spoken readings carry the translation to people who cannot read both scripts.

actions.description: Councilman Geroff formally accepts the surrender on Zora's behalf within his written limited mandate. He promises survival and process, not absolution or instant peace.
The hardline generals remain seated. One removes his insignia; another turns away. The civilian gallery does not cheer until Sela hears River Gate confirm that soldiers have left the pumps.

pages.title: THE END OF THE DEMON WARS

source_visual_beats.description: Cease-fire orders travel by radio, rail runner, balloon signal, and mounted courier. Confirmations return unevenly from the districts and frontier units.

At River Gate, clean water enters the Low Basin main. It is rationed, imperfect, and real. Midori watches without touching the crystal bank. She asks Sela for the ledger instead of assuming the next use of her power belongs to her.

source_visual_beats.description: Buren helps Sela guide a Nyssarian utility walker through rubble. A soldier thanks him.

May Jin leaves the chamber with Lian and their younger child beside him, the search for his parents and older child still unfinished and suspicion still following behind. M’ow Oh enters custody. Midori speaks Adnil’s and Marta’s names without turning them into an order for revenge; grief remains, and the next choice will still have to be made rather than assumed.

dialogue.speaker: Buren
segments: Do not mistake help for forgiveness.
Help comes first.
